about: Read the photo (#198, #249, #281, #283): the most of each unit a recipe line plausibly asks for. A photo-read line that starts with an amount and its unit (an ingredient line, or a step shaped like one, such as a glaze's lines after the method) whose amount is above its unit's maximum ('34 tsp salt', '23 cups oats': a fraction glyph read as digits) is listed for the cook to check, with its own note ('This amount looks large: check it'); the heading 'the photo was hard to read there' shows only when another line is listed for another reason. Flagged only: nothing is suggested or corrected, and the scaler reads the number as written. Keyed by the unit the language's units.json names the unit word as (MeasureUnit), so it is language-independent; a unit not listed (VARIES), a bare count ('12 eggs'), a 'Step 4' line, a line holding '=' and a language whose amounts follow the name (Japanese) are never checked. fractionShapes are the digits a recipe's fraction glyphs read as when the slash is lost (½ 12, ⅓ 13, ¼ 14, ⅛ 18, ⅔ 23, ¾ 34, ⅜ 38, ⅝ 58, ⅞ 78; fifths and sixths, never written in the calibration pages, are left out, so '16 tablespoons' and '15 g' stay plain numbers). An amount written exactly so is never taken for a temperature ('1 58 C sugar' is 1 ⅝ cups), and is judged by its unit's fractionShapedMaximums, a lower bar, where one is listed ('12 tbsp vinegar' for ½), else by maximums; ounces, grams and millilitres have none, since '12 oz', '14 g' and '15 ml' are everyday amounts. Either end of a range ('12–14 lb') is judged by maximums only. Every maximum must be a JSON number above 0 and every fraction shape a JSON string of digits: anything else stops the app, on both platforms, as any malformed table does. Calibrated so no real ingredient or instruction line in the repo's fixtures and saved pages is flagged (docs/decisions.md, #249, #281, #283). Applies to photo-read lines only, never to a parsed web recipe.
